subject: Chemistry
solution:
Concept: In the iodoform test, $\mathrm{I_2}$ or hypoiodite ($\mathrm{OI^-}$) is formed in the presence of base. It oxidises and iodinates a $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group, or a $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ group that can be oxidised to $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$, giving yellow $\mathrm{CHI_3}$.
Statement A: $\mathrm{NaOCl + KI \rightarrow KOI + NaCl}$. Hypochlorite oxidises iodide to hypoiodite, so A is true.
Statement B: In $\mathrm{KOI}$, iodine is in the $+1$ state. It oxidises the substrate and is reduced to $\mathrm{I^-}$, so it is an oxidising agent, not a reducing agent. B is false.
Statement C: The figure shows $\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH{=}CH{-}CO{-}CH_3}$. It contains a $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group, so it forms $\mathrm{CHI_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCOO^-}$. C is true.
Statement D: Isopropyl alcohol, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHOH}$, is oxidised to acetone, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$, which gives iodoform. So it gives a positive test, and D is false.
Statement E: Methanoic acid, $\mathrm{HCOOH}$, has neither a $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group nor a $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ group, so it gives a negative test. E is false.
The true statements are A and C.
Answer: (D) A & C Only
